stories.title: Burnham at PMQs: 'National security can't come at expense of social security'
stories.summary: Andy Burnham faced Kemi Badenoch at PMQs, declaring that increasing defence spending must not come at the cost of welfare and public services. He defended his position on both national security and cost-of-living support.

stories.title: Burnham says he would consider Scottish independence referendum if there is 'clear consensus'
stories.summary: In a shift from previous messaging that indyref2 was 'off limits', PM Burnham signalled at PMQs that a second independence referendum would be considered if there is a clear majority of public support. First Minister Swinney welcomed the comments.

stories.title: 'Mr Congeniality' Burnham advises Badenoch to ditch the point-scoring on defence
stories.summary: Following PMQs, Burnham publicly advised Kemi Badenoch to work cross-party on defence rather than pursue political point-scoring, citing the seriousness of national security challenges facing the UK.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 Burnham raises AI security threat at PMQs; Anthropic declines UK AI safety testing
stories.summary: PM Burnham flagged at PMQs that AI poses a threat to national security, responding to an FT story that Anthropic declined to submit its latest model to Britain's AI Security Institute under US pressure. He called for a cross-party approach to AI governance.

stories.title: 🤖 GDS talent team preps vendor training, pay reform plans, and returnship scheme
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service's talent team is developing new vendor training programmes, pay reform initiatives, and a returnship scheme aimed at addressing digital skills gaps across the civil service.

stories.title: 🤖 Experts find MPs are using AI for parliamentary submissions — and denying it
stories.summary: A new study found evidence that Members of Parliament are using AI tools to draft parliamentary submissions while publicly denying it, raising questions about transparency and authenticity in democratic processes.

stories.title: 🏗️ UK Biobank awards £364k threat-intelligence contract following data breach
stories.summary: UK Biobank, a major public health research body, awarded a £364,000 contract for threat intelligence services in the wake of a recent data breach, signalling heightened cyber security spending across public sector research bodies.

stories.title: 🤖 New national space strategy: £7.8bn investment to 2030 with security focus (UKAuthority)
stories.summary: The government unveiled a new national space strategy with £7.8 billion in investment until 2030, with a strong emphasis on security, defence and technological advancement, including satellite-guided infrastructure and earth observation.

stories.title: 🤝 Accenture adds Gemini Enterprise Business Group to its reinvention (TechMarketView)
stories.summary: Accenture has established a new Gemini Enterprise Business Group as part of its ongoing AI-led reinvention strategy, signalling continued major consulting firm investment in Google AI tools for enterprise and government clients.

stories.title: 🏗️ Palantir's NESO extension exposes grid dependency problem (TechMarketView)
stories.summary: TechMarketView reports that Palantir's extension with the National Energy System Operator (NESO) has highlighted deep government dependency on a single vendor for critical national energy grid data and analytics, raising strategic concerns.

stories.title: 📄 Research Report — Building No. 10 North (re-state.co.uk): Key Insights
stories.summary: Re:State think tank paper argues No. 10 North must be a 'testbed for radically different governance' with a PM's Transformation Directorate and four core units — not symbolism. PM priorities identified: reindustrialisation, radical devolution, public ownership of utilities, local regeneration. Success metric: No. 10 North's central functions become unnecessary as devolution matures.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs & Legislation

stories.title: PMQs: Burnham vs Badenoch clash on defence, spending and cost of living
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced Kemi Badenoch at PMQs, defending his balanced approach to national security and social security while pushing back on Conservative attacks over borrowing costs and welfare reform.

stories.title: Equalities Minister Phillipson to make Commons announcement on equalities plans
stories.summary: Equalities Minister Bridget Phillipson is set to deliver a written statement to the House of Commons announcing new government plans on women and equalities policy.

stories.title: Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill gets second reading
stories.summary: The Civil Aviation Bill received its second reading in the House of Commons as part of the Burnham Government's early legislative agenda, alongside debate on ticket price regulation for live events.

stories.title: Labour selects former child refugee Sagal Abdi-Wali for Holborn & St Pancras by-election
stories.summary: Labour has chosen Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali, who came to the UK from Somalia as a child refugee in the 1990s, as its candidate for the Holborn & St Pancras by-election in the seat vacated by Keir Starmer.

stories.title: TUC leader warns Burnham against political donations cap — 'a step backwards'
stories.summary: TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak warned PM Burnham that a cap on political donations would be 'a step backwards' and silence union members' democratic voice, amid reports the government is considering the policy.

stories.title: Think tank urges Burnham to tackle inequality with wealth tax and other bold policies
stories.summary: Progressive think tank Compass published a report urging PM Burnham to take bolder action on inequality, including a wealth tax, as pressure mounts from Labour's left flank not to 'appease the right' or follow Reform's shadow.

stories.title: Badenoch brands Burnham 'continuity Keir' at PMQs — PM fires back
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch attacked Andy Burnham at PMQs as 'continuity Keir', claiming he is repeating Starmer's failed approach. Burnham pushed back, highlighting differences in his government's direction.

stories.title: Badenoch faced criticism for being 'on wrong side' of West Bank sanctions debate
stories.summary: Following PMQs, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch was criticised internally and by commentators for appearing to take the wrong side of public opinion on the government's decision to impose sanctions on Israeli West Bank settlements.

stories.title: Ed Davey thanks PM Burnham for Israel sanctions — Lib Dems back government position
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey thanked PM Burnham at PMQs for implementing West Bank sanctions, signalling Lib Dem support for the government's foreign policy stance on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

stories.title: Met Police launch criminal investigation into Reform UK overseas donations
stories.summary: Scotland Yard confirmed it is broadening its investigation into Reform UK following a Channel 4 News undercover sting showing senior party figures discussing ways to circumvent electoral law with an apparent foreign donor. Two close Farage advisers resigned last week.

stories.title: Farage: 'I wasn't even listening' during foreign donor talks filmed undercover
stories.summary: Nigel Farage told the BBC he was not listening during conversations captured on undercover video showing his team discussing illegal foreign donations, as Reform said it would 'fully cooperate' with the Metropolitan Police investigation.

stories.title: Reform UK insists French National Rally agreed migrant policy — Paris denies it
stories.summary: Reform UK claimed National Rally leader Jordan Bardella signed a memorandum agreeing to return Channel migrants intercepted in British waters to France. French politicians and officials rejected the account, causing a diplomatic row.

stories.title: Burnham signals he'd consider indyref2 if 'clear majority of public support' exists
stories.summary: PM Burnham softened his previous 'off limits' position on Scottish independence, telling PMQs he would consider a second referendum if there is a clear majority of public support — a significant shift welcomed by First Minister Swinney.

stories.title: MPs launch party funding inquiry following Peter Murrell SNP embezzlement scandal
stories.summary: The Scottish Affairs Committee announced inquiries into party political funding following the conviction of Peter Murrell, former SNP chief executive, for embezzlement of party funds — a long-running scandal that has damaged the SNP's reputation.

stories.title: MoJ deploys PolyAI Luna conversational AI tool — algorithmic transparency record published
stories.summary: The Ministry of Justice published an algorithmic transparency record for its PolyAI Luna AI deployment, coordinated through the Cabinet Office and Government Digital Service — marking another step in government AI accountability measures.

stories.title: Chancellor to unveil £150m fund for fast-growing northern companies
stories.summary: The Chancellor is set to announce a £150 million investment fund targeting fast-growing companies in northern England, aligning with PM Burnham's reindustrialisation and levelling up agenda.

stories.title: Labour selects Sagal Abdi-Wali for Holborn & St Pancras by-election — Starmer's old seat
stories.summary: Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the Holborn & St Pancras by-election triggered by Keir Starmer's departure from Parliament.

stories.title: Green leader Zack Polanski aims to win Holborn & St Pancras by-election
stories.summary: Green Party leader Zack Polanski is standing in the Holborn & St Pancras by-election hoping to take Starmer's old seat, making it high-stakes for both Labour and the Greens in what could be a bellwether for Burnham's popularity.

stories.title: Holborn & St Pancras by-election: 'Labour's to lose' but Green challenge is real
stories.summary: Commentary and analysis suggests Labour should hold the seat but the Green Party is mounting a credible challenge on defence, energy and housing issues that have put pressure on Burnham's left flank.

stories.title: More than 100 peers call on colleagues to 'complete the task' on assisted dying bill
stories.summary: Over 100 members of the House of Lords signed an open letter urging fellow peers to vote to complete the passage of the assisted dying bill, amid ongoing debate over its final provisions.

stories.title: Lords debate AI and essential services under new Cyber Security Bill
stories.summary: The House of Lords debated provisions of the Cyber Security Bill relating to AI use in essential national services, with peers raising concerns about accountability and vendor lock-in in critical infrastructure.
